title: Bake reusable radial halo texture via Pixmap (port VFXPool haloTexture / soft-dot)
description:
BACKGROUND: iOS VFXPool.swift lines 28-47 lazily build a single 256x256 radial-gradient SKTexture (white-center alpha=1 -> transparent edge alpha=0, 2-stop CGGradient over deviceRGB, drawn with CGContext.drawRadialGradient) and cache it as a static. ThrusterEmitter.swift lines 75-98 builds a similar 32px soft dot but with a 3-stop ramp (alpha 1.0 @0, 0.6 @0.5, 0.0 @1.0). Both are used everywhere as the soft additive glow primitive; the comment notes the bundled Glow.imageset asset was a fully-opaque white square that read as a colored box under additive blend, so a baked radial gradient is mandatory.

TASK: Create core/.../render/HaloTextures.kt (Kotlin object). Bake two textures ONCE at construction and reuse for the whole app lifetime:
  1) halo256: 256x256 RGBA8888 Pixmap, 2-stop radial gradient white(a=255)@center -> white(a=0)@radius=128.
  2) softDot32: 32x32 RGBA8888 Pixmap, 3-stop radial gradient a=255 @0, a=153 (0.6*255) @ r=8 (0.5), a=0 @ r=16.
Use a manual per-pixel loop computing distance from center: for each (x,y), d = dist/maxRadius clamped to [0,1]; interpolate alpha across the stops; RGB stays white (255,255,255). Wrap each Pixmap in a Texture with TextureFilter.Linear (the halo is scaled up large; iOS leaves halo at default filtering). Dispose Pixmaps after upload; expose Texture (or a TextureRegion) getters. Provide a dispose() for the Textures.

MAPPING: SKTexture(image: CG radial gradient) -> Pixmap + Texture. CGGradient 2-stop -> manual lerp. UIGraphicsImageRenderer -> Pixmap. blendMode .add at draw time (not baked) -> caller sets SpriteBatch.setBlendFunction(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE) when drawing halos.

ACCEPTANCE: object compiles; halo256 and softDot32 expose non-null Textures; a debug draw shows a soft circular falloff (no hard square edge); center pixel alpha==255, corner pixel alpha==0. No per-frame allocation — textures created exactly once.

title: VFXPool.kt: muzzle flash, damage flash, glow halo, blackhole warp (port VFXPool.swift)
description:
BACKGROUND: Port GalaxyMonkey/VFXPool.swift (168 lines). It owns four transient one-shot effects, all drawn with the baked halo texture under additive blend. LibGDX has no SKAction/scene graph, so model each live effect as a lightweight struct in a list that VFXPool.update(dt) advances and VFXPool.render(batch) draws; recycle structs via the track2 object pool (no per-spawn GC churn).

EFFECTS TO PORT (constants live verbatim in Tuning.VFX from track2-tuning):
  1) spawnMuzzleFlash(x,y,angleRad): halo sprite tinted (1.0,0.92,0.55), colorBlendFactor 0.7 (lerp texture-white toward tint), additive, scale so display size = Player.radius*2*muzzleFlashScale(0.6), rotation=angle, z=48, fadeOut over muzzleFlashDuration(0.08s) then remove. iOS lines 51-69.
  2) spawnDamageFlash(target): tint a target sprite white (colorBlendFactor 1.0) instantly then ramp blendFactor back to 0 over damageFlashDuration(0.12s). In LibGDX, sprites are drawn by their owning system, so expose a 'damageFlash timer' on the entity (Player/Enemy carry a flashTimer field) and have VFX set it; the entity's renderer lerps its color toward white by remaining timer/duration. iOS lines 71-83. Coordinate field name with track5 (player/enemytype).
  3) spawnGlow(x,y,scale,duration,color default (1.0,0.85,0.4)): halo, colorBlendFactor 0.8, additive, size = Enemy.radius*2*scale, z=49, fadeOut over duration. iOS lines 85-103.
  4) spawnBlackholeWarp(enemyDrawData, x,y): kid-friendly enemy death. Spawn a soft violet halo (tint (0.55,0.20,0.85), blendFactor 0.9, additive, z=44, size=Enemy.radius*2*blackholeScale(3.0)) that fades 0->0.7 over blackholeOpenDuration(0.15), holds warpFadeDuration*0.4, then fades out over blackholeCollapseDuration(0.2); the halo slowly spins -2pi over blackholeSpinPeriod(1.0s). Concurrently the dying enemy sprite: colorize toward violet (0.62,0.20,0.95) blendFactor 0.7 over warpVioletDuration(0.12), then after that delay group(scale->0.05, alpha->0) over warpFadeDuration(0.3) with easeInOut, then the effect owns removing the enemy from the active list. iOS lines 111-166.

MAPPING: SKAction.fadeOut/scale/colorize/rotate sequences -> per-effect interpolated timers in update(dt). SKAction.sequence -> phase state machine (e.g. enum {VIOLET, DISSOLVE, DONE}). easeInEaseOut -> Interpolation.smooth or smoothstep helper. blendMode .add -> batch.setBlendFunction(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE) for the additive pass, restore default after. colorBlendFactor -> tint = lerp(Color.WHITE, tintColor, factor) applied via batch.setColor.

ORDERING: additive halos (muzzle/glow/blackhole) should draw in their own additive pass after world sprites; damage flash is handled inline by the entity renderer. VFXPool exposes renderAdditive(batch) so GameScreen can call it at the right z-band.

ACCEPTANCE: spawning each effect adds a pooled struct; update advances and auto-frees on completion (no leak — pool free-list returns to its prior size after the effect's lifetime); blackhole warp removes its enemy after the full sequence; rendering uses additive blend then restores default. No allocation in spawn after warmup.

title: ThrusterEmitter.kt: rocket exhaust plume, color ramp, stick-driven birthrate (port ThrusterEmitter.swift)
description:
BACKGROUND: Port GalaxyMonkey/ThrusterEmitter.swift (100 lines), an SKEmitterNode chemical-rocket plume behind the ship. SpriteKit's emitter has no LibGDX 1:1; choose ONE of: (a) a manual particle system backed by the track2 pool (recommended — full control over the exact iOS params), or (b) libGDX ParticleEffect tuned to match. Document the choice in the bead. The plume must mirror the ship's facing automatically (iOS emits toward local -X / emissionAngle=pi, and the ship's xScale flip mirrors it).

iOS PARAMETERS TO REPRODUCE (lines 23-71): particleBirthRate cruise 220 (Player.update modulates it each frame — see modulation below); particleLifetime 0.45 +/- 0.15; emissionAngle pi (rear) with emissionAngleRange pi/9 (~+/-20deg spread); particleSpeed 200 +/- 70; particlePositionRange dx=2, dy=14 (covers both nozzles); COLOR RAMP keyframes white-hot->orange->red->smoke at times [0.0,0.2,0.45,0.75,1.0]: (1.00,1.00,0.85), (1.00,0.78,0.20), (1.00,0.35,0.05), (0.40,0.20,0.10), (0.18,0.18,0.18); particleScale = Tuning.VFX.thrustScale(1.4)*0.5 +/- 0.25, scaleSpeed -0.6 (shrinks as it cools); particleAlpha 1.0 +/- 0.1, alphaSpeed -2.2 (fades out by end of life); blendMode .add; texture = softDot32 from track6-halo-texture.

BIRTHRATE/SPEED MODULATION: the comment 'birthrate driven by stick magnitude'. Expose setIntensity(mag: Float in [0,1]) that scales birthRate from a cruise idle floor up to full burst and bumps particleSpeed. Player.kt (track5) feeds the joystick magnitude (track4-joystick) each frame. Pick a sane mapping (e.g. birthRate = lerp(cruise*0.4, cruise*1.5, mag); speed = lerp(160, 240, mag)) and document it; cruise=220 is the iOS baseline.

PLACEMENT: emitter sits at thrustTailOffsetX(-22) along the ship's local +X (i.e. behind), z = thrustZ(-1, just under the body). Position/rotate with the ship each frame.

MAPPING: SKKeyframeSequence -> sample the 5-stop ramp by particle age fraction (binary-search or linear scan + lerp). particleScaleSpeed/alphaSpeed (per-second deltas) -> integrate over dt. emissionAngleRange -> random within +/- range. blendMode .add -> additive batch pass.

ACCEPTANCE: at idle the plume is thin; ramping intensity to 1 thickens and brightens it; particle colors progress white->orange->red->smoke over life; particles fade and shrink to nothing by lifetime end; emitter mirrors when the ship faces left; particles are pooled (no per-particle GC after warmup).

title: Starfield.kt: two baked parallax layers, 3x3 wrapping tiles, screen-locked twinkle (port Starfield.swift)
description:
BACKGROUND: Port GalaxyMonkey/Starfield.swift (203 lines). Two baked parallax star layers tiled 3x3 around the camera so they wrap seamlessly, plus a screen-locked async twinkle pass. iOS renders these in CAMERA-LOCAL (screen) space attached to SKCameraNode; in LibGDX with an OrthographicCamera the equivalent is to draw with a screen-space/UI batch (or convert camera position deltas) so stars wrap relative to the camera, NOT the world.

PARAMETERS (Tuning.Starfield from track2): layer1 80 dots, radius 1.4, alpha 0.65, parallaxFactor 0.06, z=-50 (deep/slow). layer2 30 dots, radius 2.2, alpha 0.95, parallaxFactor 0.18, z=-49 (closer/brighter). twinkle: count 16, radius 1.6, alphaLow 0.3, period random 1.2..3.5s.

BAKED TILE (iOS bakeStarTexture lines 182-202): per layer, create ONE tile texture sized to the viewport (max(64,viewW) x max(64,viewH)), fill N random white ellipses at the given radius/alpha. Use a Pixmap (fillCircle) -> Texture with TextureFilter.Nearest (iOS sets filteringMode .nearest). Make 9 sprites sharing that texture for a 3x3 grid.

PARALLAX + WRAP (iOS update lines 49-82): take cameraDelta = camera.position - lastCameraPosition (world space) each frame. Each layer accumulates offset -= cameraDelta * (1 - parallaxFactor). Wrap offset into [-tileSize, tileSize] with a while-loop. Then place the 9 tiles at grid cell (gx,gy in -1..1): pos = (gx*tw + offset.x, gy*th + offset.y), centered on the camera origin (anchor 0.5,0.5).

TWINKLE (iOS installTwinkle lines 117-141): 16 white dots at random screen positions, each fading between full alpha and alphaLow(0.3) on its own random period (1.2..3.5s) with easeInOut, random initial phase so they desync. No parallax. Model each as {x,y,period,phase} and compute alpha = lerp(low,1.0, smooth(triangle(phase + t)/...)) each frame; draw screen-locked.

REBUILD (iOS rebuild lines 85-110): on viewport resize/rotation, dispose old textures and re-bake. Provide resize(w,h).

MAPPING: SKCameraNode-attached node -> draw in a screen-space pass (batch with screen projection) so wrapping is camera-relative. CGContext fillEllipse -> Pixmap.fillCircle. SKShapeNode circle (twinkle) -> small soft dot or filled circle texture. SKAction fade loop -> per-dot sinusoid/triangle in update.

ACCEPTANCE: panning the camera scrolls layer2 faster than layer1 (parallax read); no seams/gaps appear as the 3x3 grid wraps (offset stays bounded); twinkle dots pulse asynchronously and stay fixed to the viewport; resize re-bakes without leaking the old textures (dispose called).

title: PlanetField.kt: solar orrery scene graph — sun, 8 planets, moons, rings, orbit ticking (port PlanetField.swift, static shading)
description:
BACKGROUND: Port GalaxyMonkey/PlanetField.swift (410 lines) WITHOUT the terminator shader for now (static shading) — the shader is split into track6-planetfield-shader as the riskiest piece. This bead builds the full orrery structure and motion. The Sun sits at worldCenter; every planet starts at phase 0 (opening conjunction line) then drifts apart at its own angular speed. Orbits are co-planar on a tilted ecliptic (orbitTiltY=0.45 squashes Y).

STRUCTURE (iOS init lines 83-153): root node at scene center. For each orbital body keep an Orbit{node/transform, radius, phase, angularSpeed, optional bodySprite, optional frontZ/backZ}. Build order matters for z-layering:
  - installSun (lines 202-244): sun sprite scaled to sunDisplayDiameter(600); a blurred additive corona behind it (z=-46.5) that pulses scale (amp/period from Tuning.World.sunCorona*) — for LibGDX use the baked halo (track6-halo) or a pre-blurred texture as the corona since SKEffectNode CIGaussianBlur has no cheap equivalent; sun spins slowly (planetRotationPeriodMin..Max 60..180s). z sun=-46.
  - 8 orbit rings (installOrbitRing lines 190-200): tilted ellipses (ShapeRenderer or a baked ring texture), strokeColor white*orbitRingAlpha, z=-47.
  - 8 planets (installPlanet lines 249-283): each on an unscaled pivot carrying the orbit; body sprite scaled to its diameter, alpha 0.95, slow self-rotation random period/direction. z from -45 (mercury) to -38 (neptune). Mercury gets behindSunZ=-46.7 (frontZ/backZ flip — far side y>=0 draws behind the sun).
  - moons (installMoon lines 289-309): Luna on Earth; Io/Europa/Ganymede/Callisto on Jupiter; Titan on Saturn. Moons are children of the planet pivot (unscaled frame), random start phase, z=0.1 above the body.

description:

title: PlanetField comets: timed chord-streak with detached additive trail (port spawnComet)
description:
BACKGROUND: Port the comet system from PlanetField.swift spawnComet (lines 316-361) and its countdown driver in update (lines 181-185). A comet periodically streaks across the world on a straight chord, trailing additive particles that DETACH into world space (no tail dragged with the head) for a streak look.

LOGIC: cometCountdown starts at World.cometInitialDelay, decrements by dt; when <=0 spawn a comet and reset to random(cometSpawnIntervalMin..Max). spawnComet: pick entryAngle random[0,2pi), exitAngle = entry + pi + jitter(+/-cometExitJitterRad); start/end points on an ellipse of radius cometPathRadius squashed by orbitTiltY. Head = small white additive circle (cometHeadRadius), z=-42.5. Trail = particle emitter using the halo texture (track6-halo), birthRate cometTrailBirthRate, lifetime cometTrailLifetime, alpha 0.9 alphaSpeed -0.6, scale 0.18 scaleSpeed -0.08, color (0.82,0.95,1.0) blendFactor 0.85, additive, particleSpeed 0; CRUCIAL: trail particles are emitted into WORLD space (iOS targetNode=root) so they stay put as the head moves. The comet follows the chord (orientToPath) over random(cometTravelDurationMin..Max) then removes itself.

MAPPING: SKAction.follow(path, orientToPath) -> lerp head position start->end over duration, set rotation = atan2(dir). targetNode=root (detached particles) -> spawn trail particles into a world-space particle list owned by PlanetField, NOT parented to the moving head; each particle decays independently via track2 pool. SKEmitterNode -> manual pooled particles (reuse the thruster approach) or a small ParticleEffect.

ACCEPTANCE: a comet appears after the initial delay and at random intervals; it crosses the play area on a chord; the trail is left BEHIND as a fading streak (particles do not follow the head); head and trail use additive blend; the comet despawns at path end and frees its particles (no leak).

  - chord geometry: start and end points lie on the tilted ellipse (radius cometPathRadius, Y squashed by orbitTiltY); the angle between entry and exit is pi +/- cometExitJitterRad.
  - head motion: at t=0 head at start, at t=duration head at end, linear in between; rotation == atan2(end-start).
  - detached trail: emit particles while moving, then teleport the head; previously emitted particles DO NOT move with the head (assert a sampled particle's world position is unchanged after the head moves). Particles free back to the pool after cometTrailLifetime.

title: PlanetField terminator shader: port GLSL to LibGDX ShaderProgram with static-shading fallback (riskiest bead)
description:
BACKGROUND: RISKIEST BEAD. Port the day/night terminator shader from PlanetField.swift lines 59-77 and its per-frame sun-angle update (lines 169-179) to a LibGDX ShaderProgram applied to each planet body sprite. iOS SKShader uses SpriteKit's implicit varyings (v_tex_coord, u_texture) and a per-sprite SKAttribute a_sun_angle; LibGDX SpriteBatch shaders use a_position/a_texCoord0/a_color attributes, u_projTrans, u_texture, and you must pass a_sun_angle as a per-draw UNIFORM (SpriteBatch cannot supply per-vertex custom attributes easily) — so each planet is drawn in its own batch.setShader call with shader.setUniformf("u_sunAngle", angle) before drawing that sprite.

GLSL TO PORT (fragment): base = texture2D(u_texture, v_texCoord); centered = v_texCoord - 0.5; sunDir = vec2(cos(u_sunAngle), sin(u_sunAngle)); d = dot(normalize(centered + vec2(1e-4)), sunDir); lit = smoothstep(-0.4, 0.4, d); gl_FragColor = vec4(base.rgb * mix(0.28, 1.04, lit), base.a) * v_color. (Keep the *v_color so SpriteBatch tint/alpha still works — planet alpha is 0.95.) Provide a matching trivial vertex shader (standard SpriteBatch passthrough).

PER-FRAME ANGLE (iOS lines 169-179): for each planet, sunLocal = phase + pi - bodySelfRotation (the sun is at world origin, planet at angle phase; subtract the planet's own spin so the lit side stays world-fixed while the surface spins). Wire PlanetField.update to compute this and the renderer to set the uniform per planet.

FALLBACK (MANDATORY): add a boolean Tuning/Settings flag (e.g. terminatorShaderEnabled, default true). On ShaderProgram compile failure (check shader.isCompiled — log shader.log) OR when the flag is false, fall back to STATIC shading: draw the planet sprite with the plain default batch shader at alpha 0.95 (exactly what track6-planetfield-orrery already does). This guarantees planets always render even on a GPU/driver that rejects the shader. Log the chosen path once at init.

MAPPING: SKShader source -> ShaderProgram(vert, frag). SKAttribute a_sun_angle (per-sprite) -> per-draw uniform u_sunAngle (one setShader+draw per planet). v_tex_coord -> v_texCoord0 from the vertex shader. u_texture stays. blend stays normal (terminator multiplies brightness, not additive).

ACCEPTANCE: with the shader on, each planet shows a soft lit/dark terminator band whose lit side faces the sun and stays world-fixed as the planet spins; smoothstep(-0.4,0.4) gives a wide twilight band (not a hard line); night side keeps brightness 0.28 (still readable); day side ~1.04. With the flag off OR on compile failure, planets render flat at alpha 0.95 and the game does not crash. The chosen path is logged.

title: Test: terminator shader compiles + correct sun-angle math + fallback path

Test split into GL-required and pure-logic parts. PURE LOGIC (headless, no GL): test sunLocalAngle(phase, selfRotation) == phase + PI - selfRotation, and that for a body with selfRotation increasing, the WORLD-space lit direction (sunLocal + selfRotation) stays constant == phase + PI (the lit side is world-fixed while the surface spins) — assert across several spin values. Verify smoothstep mapping at the GLSL level by replicating it in Kotlin: lit(d) for d=-0.4 -> 0, d=0.4 -> 1, d=0 -> 0.5; brightness = mix(0.28,1.04,lit) so night(d<=-0.4)=0.28, day(d>=0.4)=1.04.

GL PART (HeadlessApplication with a GL context if available in CI; otherwise guard/skip and assert via shader.isCompiled in an instrumented run): compile the ShaderProgram and assert shader.isCompiled == true; if false, log shader.log and assert the fallback flag flips to static shading (no crash). Assert the init log line states which path was taken.

LOGGING EXPECTATIONS: log 'terminator sunLocal phase=%.2f spin=%.2f -> local=%.2f worldLit=%.2f', 'terminator brightness d=%.2f lit=%.2f bright=%.2f', and 'terminator path=%s (shader|static) compiled=%b log=%s' so a shader compile failure on a real device is fully explained by the log and the fallback is provably exercised.

title: Wire VFX/Thruster/Starfield/PlanetField into GameScreen render order and lifecycle
description:
BACKGROUND: Integrate all track6 renderers into the GameScreen draw loop with correct z-banding mirroring the iOS zPosition layering, and into the update/pause/resize/dispose lifecycle. iOS implicit z-order back-to-front: starfield layers (-50,-49) and twinkle (-48.5); planet field (sun corona -46.5, sun -46, rings -47, planets -45..-38, moons +0.1 local, asteroids -41.5, comets -42.5); world entities (player/enemies/projectiles); additive VFX halos (muzzle 48, glow 49, blackhole 44). Replicate this ordering in a single render pass sequence in GameScreen.

TASK: In GameScreen.render(dt) (track3-gamescreen): (1) update all: planetField.update(dt), starfield.update(dt, cameraDelta from track3-camera), vfxPool.update(dt), thruster intensity from player. (2) draw in order: starfield (screen-space, behind world) -> planetField (world space, behind entities; uses normal blend; planets via shader/fallback, corona+comets additive) -> entity layer (player incl. thruster plume just under body z=thrustZ -1) -> additive VFX pass (vfxPool.renderAdditive). (3) Respect pause: per the project's prior fix, freeze gameplay tick while paused — starfield twinkle and planet orbits should also pause (do not advance update(dt) when paused) so nothing marches behind menus. (4) resize -> starfield.rebuild(w,h); planetField recompute center if needed. (5) dispose -> dispose all baked textures (halo, star tiles) and the shader.

MAPPING: SKScene addChild + zPosition -> explicit ordered draw calls with the right batch/blend state per band; switch blend to additive only for the halo/corona/comet bands then restore. SKCameraNode-relative starfield -> screen-space batch projection. Pause freeze -> guard update(dt) calls behind the paused flag (matches commit 50697c0 'freeze gameplay tick while paused').

ACCEPTANCE: full scene renders back-to-front matching iOS; thruster sits under the ship; VFX halos composite additively on top; pausing freezes orbits/twinkle/VFX; resize re-bakes starfield without artifacts; dispose releases all GPU resources (no leak warnings).

(4) Resize to a new viewport: starfield rebuild invoked, no crash, offsets re-bounded. (5) dispose: all baked textures + shader disposed exactly once (no double-dispose, no leak).

title: SettingsStore.kt backed by LibGDX Preferences
description: Port GalaxyMonkey/SettingsStore.swift (61 lines) to core/ as SettingsStore.kt. iOS uses UserDefaults; the LibGDX equivalent is Gdx.app.getPreferences("galaxymonkey.settings") returning a Preferences instance. SETTINGS PORTED: three persisted keys with exact string names from the iOS Keys enum so saves are conceptually identical — "settings.musicVolume" (Float), "settings.sfxVolume" (Float), "settings.hapticsEnabled" (Boolean). Mirror this with prefs.contains(key): if !contains -> return Tuning default, else prefs.getFloat/getBoolean(key). musicVolume and sfxVolume SETTERS clamp to [0,1] via coerceIn(0f,1f) (iOS uses max(0,min(1,newValue))) and call prefs.putFloat then prefs.flush() so the value persists immediately. hapticsEnabled setter writes the raw bool and flushes. Provide a convenience constructor or factory taking the prefs name so production code does SettingsStore(Gdx.app.getPreferences(...)) while tests can inject a fake Preferences. ACCEPTANCE: fresh store (no prefs written) returns 0.18f/1.0f/true; after setting musicVolume=2.0f, getter returns 1.0f (clamped) and survives a new SettingsStore over the same Preferences; setting hapticsEnabled=false persists across instances. title: Document gravity-integration / physics-pause ordering contract
description:
## Background

`update(_:)` in `GameScene.swift` has the structure:
1. Compute `dt`
2. Update `lastUpdateTime`
3. `guard isStarted, !isGameOver else { return }`
4. Movement, spawning, gravity integration, landing checks
5. Score update

When the penguin dies, `didBegin(_:)` (called from SpriteKit's contact resolution, which runs AFTER `update(_:)` in the same frame) sets `isGameOver = true` and `physicsWorld.speed = 0`. The next frame's `update(_:)` correctly early-returns, and `physicsWorld.speed = 0` halts SpriteKit's integration.

The latent issue: this ordering is implicit. If someone moves `integrateCustomGravity` and `checkIcicleLandings` OUTSIDE the `isStarted/!isGameOver` guard (e.g., to support a pause animation, or refactors update for clarity), one frame of post-death physics integration would occur.

## Fix (pick one)

**Option A — tombstone comment on update(_:):**
```swift
// IMPORTANT: All per-frame physics work must stay BEHIND the
// isStarted/!isGameOver guard. didBegin runs inside SpriteKit's
// physics step (AFTER update returns), so on the death frame we've
// already executed update(); we rely on the next frame's guard to
// halt further integration.
```

**Option B — restructure into a helper that no-ops when paused:**
```swift
override func update(_ currentTime: TimeInterval) {
    let dt = ...
    lastUpdateTime = currentTime
    runGameTick(dt: dt)
}

private func runGameTick(dt: TimeInterval) {
    guard isStarted, !isGameOver else { return }
    movePenguin(dt: dt, tilt: readTilt())
    maybeSpawn(dt: dt)
    integrateCustomGravity(dt: dt)
    checkIcicleLandings()
    score = Int(elapsed * 10)
}
```

Recommend Option B if Bead #6 (refactor) happens; Option A as a safety net otherwise.

## Acceptance

The dependency on guard-ordering is documented OR the structure makes the safety property local (a reader can verify it without reading the whole update loop).

## Files

PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift
close_reason: Added a docstring on update(_:) (GameScene.swift ~line 401) calling out the ordering contract: all per-frame physics work must stay behind the isStarted/!isGameOver guard, because didBegin runs INSIDE SpriteKit's physics step (after update returns) on the death frame. The next frame's guard plus physicsWorld.speed=0 halts motion. Also opportunistically cleaned up two stale doc comments at :190 and :495 that still referenced the old userData['gravity'] approach (replaced upstream by FallingBody) — they now reference integrateAndCheckLandings(dt:) and FallingBody entries respectively.

title: Make lastUpdateTime restart-safe
description:
## Background

`lastUpdateTime` is initialized to 0 at scene construction. The check `lastUpdateTime == 0 ? 0 : (currentTime - lastUpdateTime)` produces dt = 0 on the very first frame ever, then normal dt thereafter. The assignment `lastUpdateTime = currentTime` runs every frame BEFORE the isStarted/!isGameOver guard — meaning lastUpdateTime keeps ticking even when the rest of update bails. This is why dt stays small after a long pause: the timestamp is fresh.

Currently safe. But if a future refactor moves the `lastUpdateTime = currentTime` assignment INSIDE the guard (e.g., to consolidate "do nothing while paused"), then on game-over the timestamp would freeze, and on restart the next frame would compute a huge dt (could be 10s+) and the penguin would teleport.

## Fix (defensive)

Reset `lastUpdateTime = 0` in `restart()` and on the !isStarted → isStarted transition. The 0-sentinel in the ternary already handles this — restart effectively gets a "first frame" dt = 0, which is correct.

```swift
private func restart() {
    // ... existing reset ...
    lastUpdateTime = 0
}
```

```swift
override func touchesBegan(...) {
    if !isStarted {
        isStarted = true
        lastUpdateTime = 0
        ...
    }
}
```

## Acceptance

Even if a future refactor narrows the lastUpdateTime write to inside the guard, restart and start don't produce a teleport.

## Files

PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift
close_reason: Added lastUpdateTime = 0 resets in both restart() (after leanVelocity reset) and the !isStarted→isStarted branch of touchesBegan. The dt==0 sentinel in update() then produces a correct dt=0 on the first post-transition frame instead of a possibly multi-second dt from the stale anchor. Future refactor that moves the lastUpdateTime write inside the guard can no longer teleport the penguin on restart.

title: Replace userData["gravity"] with typed FallingNode subclass
description:
## Background

Icicles (post-detach) and shards both have a per-instance gravity stored as `node.userData?["gravity"] as? CGFloat`. The integration loop in `integrateCustomGravity` looks them up by this string key. Problems:
1. Typo-unsafe: `node.userData?["graivty"]` would silently no-op (cast returns nil → skipped → icicle floats).
2. Allocates an NSMutableDictionary per node.
3. Conceptually wrong — "this node has its own gravity" is a type property, not a runtime tag.

## Fix

Add `PenguinSlide/FallingNode.swift`:

```swift
import SpriteKit

/// Sprite node that integrates its own gravity per frame via
/// the host scene's gravity-integration step. Used for icicles
/// (post-detach) and for shatter shards. Setting `gravity = 0`
/// effectively pauses gravity for that node.
final class FallingNode: SKSpriteNode {
    var gravity: CGFloat = 0
}
```

### Spawn sites
- **Icicles**: spawn as `FallingNode(texture:size:)`. Leave `gravity = 0` during warning. Set `gravity = perIcicleGravity` in the detach SKAction.run block.
- **Shards**: spawn as `FallingNode(texture:)`. Set `gravity = Tuning.sceneGravity` (or `Tuning.Icicle.sceneGravity` after Bead 7).

### Integration loop
```swift
private func integrateCustomGravity(dt: TimeInterval) {
    for child in children {
        guard let node = child as? FallingNode, node.gravity > 0,
              let body = node.physicsBody else { continue }
        body.velocity.dy -= node.gravity * CGFloat(dt)
    }
}
```

### Landing check
Replace `userData?["gravity"] != nil` with `node.gravity > 0` (after a `(node as? FallingNode)` cast).

## Acceptance

1. Zero `userData["gravity"]` references remain.
2. Adding/removing gravity-driven nodes is type-safe.
3. No behavior change.
4. Compile clean.

## Files
- PenguinSlide/FallingNode.swift (NEW)
- PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift (or IcicleSystem.swift after Bead 6)
- PenguinSlide.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj — register the new file

title: Font fallback (don't hardcode AvenirNext)

## Background

`SKLabelNode(fontNamed: "AvenirNext-Bold")` (and Heavy, Medium) is used at multiple sites. If Apple ships an iOS that drops Avenir Next, every label silently falls back to Helvetica with no warning. The fallback is acceptable visually but worth being intentional.

```swift
private static func safeFont(named: String, fallback: String = ".SFUI-Regular") -> String {

}
```

title: Skill-based scoring (close-call bonus and dodge combo)
description:
## Background

Current scoring: `score = Int(elapsed * 10)`. Pure survival time, identical for a player who hugged the edge vs. one who threaded the needle. README claims dodging is the core loop, but the score is decoupled from skill.

## Goals
1. Reward close-call dodges (icicle lands near the penguin without hitting it).
2. Combo multiplier for consecutive close calls within a short window.
3. Visible feedback (HUD combo counter when combo > 1).

## Algorithm

On icicle SHATTER event (already wired via `checkIcicleLandings`):
```swift
let dx = abs(landingPoint.x - penguin.position.x)
if dx < Tuning.Score.closeCallRadius {
    let bonus = Int(Tuning.Score.closeCallBase * comboMultiplier)
    score += bonus
    timeOfLastDodge = elapsed
    combo += 1
    hud.showCombo(combo, bonus: bonus)
}
```

Per-frame: decay combo if no close call within `Tuning.Score.comboWindow`:
```swift
if elapsed - timeOfLastDodge > Tuning.Score.comboWindow {
    combo = 0
    hud.hideCombo()
}
```

## New Tuning constants
(Inside `Tuning.Score` sub-enum if Bead 7 done; otherwise flat:)
- `closeCallRadius: CGFloat = 60` — distance from penguin x for the icicle landing to count
- `closeCallBase: Int = 50` — base bonus before multiplier
- `comboWindow: TimeInterval = 2.5` — seconds between close calls to keep the streak
- `comboMaxMultiplier: CGFloat = 5.0` — cap so it doesn't run away

## HUD additions
- Combo counter appears below score label when combo >= 2, fades after `comboWindow` of inactivity.
- Optional: bonus popup text floats up from the landing point on close call.

## Acceptance
1. Standing-still survival no longer grows score as fast as active-dodging play.
2. Combo HUD appears and increments correctly.
3. Combo resets when player gets clipped (game over) or misses the window.
4. Tuning constants are documented in README.

## Files
- PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift (or IcicleSystem.swift + HUDController.swift after Bead 6)
- README.md — add Score section to tuning table

## Notes
Scope-creep risk. Implement close-call bonus FIRST as a single commit; combo multiplier as a follow-up. Don't bundle.

title: Rename Cat struct to Category
description:
## Background

The bitmask collection for physics categories is named `Cat` (with members `Cat.penguin`, `Cat.icicle`, `Cat.shard`). Reads ambiguously — sounds like cat (animal) or cathode (ray) more than "category." No length benefit, no domain reason to abbreviate.

## Fix

Rename `Cat` → `Category`. Update all references in any file that uses it.

If done BEFORE Bead penguinslide-6 (extraction): only `PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift` is affected.

If done AFTER Bead #6: also affects `IcicleSystem.swift`, `Penguin.swift`, and any other extracted file referencing categories.

Recommend doing this BEFORE Bead #6 to minimize file-touch surface.

## Acceptance

1. Zero `Cat.` references remain.
2. No behavior change.
3. Compile clean.

## Files

PenguinSlide/GameScene.swift (+ extracted files if Bead 6 already merged)
